To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we can obtain state-of-the-art performance in relation extraction and semantic role labeling by combining a neural factor with a structured factor, (2) we can obtain a significant performance gain in semantic role labeling and a moderate gain in relation extraction by training with approximation-aware learning, and (3) we can obtain an additional performance gain in relation extraction and moderate gains in semantic role labeling by jointly modeling part-of-speech, syntax, and semantics

we can: 1) improve state-of-the-art semantic role labeling and relation extraction by modeling the inputs with neural factors, 2) jointly model part-of speech, syntactic, and semantic information in a low-resource dependency setting, and 3) learn neural models for structured prediction that are aware of the approximations made by inference.
